newsitem.title: USA: Senate expected to start nuke waste debate Mar 19.
newsitem.headline: Senate expected to start nuke waste debate Mar 19.

text.p: The U.S. Senate is expected to begin discussing a bill Wednesday to build a temporary storage facility for radioactive waste from nuclear power plants, Sen. Frank Murkowski said Monday.

The Senate Energy Committee, chaired by the Alaska Republican, approved a bill last week that would require the Clinton administration to build a temporary dump for the nuclear waste until it has a permanent repository ready.

Opponents to the legislation, led by the senators from Nevada, where the temporary dump would likely be sited, are expected to spend 30 hours fighting the start of debate on the bill, Murkowski told reporters.
"There will be extended debate on the motion to proceed (with the bill)," he said, after giving a speech to the National Ocean Industries Association.
"I hope we can get through that this week," he said, adding that the bill itself could then be debated after the Senate returns from a two-week recess, which begins next week.

Under the bill, the interim storage site would be built aboveground in Nevada near Yucca Mountain, if the government declares next year that waste could eventually be buried permanently in the mountain.
The Clinton administration has repeatedly said it does not expect to have a permanent repository ready until 2010.

But under a 1982 law, reaffirmed by a federal court last year, the government is supposed to take over control of the thousands of tons of waste building up at nuclear power plants by the end of January 1998.
